FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Short answers.
Source-linked depth.

These answers reflect current public repositories and the V4 published source release status as of 2026-10-28.

What is MESA?

MESA is open-source memory infrastructure for AI systems. Its released V4 source combines durable mutation state, structured assertions, scoped retrieval, and source provenance across versioned HTTP, Python SDK, and MCP surfaces.

Is MESA a vector database?

No. A vector database is one part inside it. MESA keeps the original record in SQLite, builds a vector index (LanceDB) and a relationship graph (Kùzu) from it, and searches all of them together.

Is MESA a RAG framework?

Not primarily. It can supply grounded context to an application, but its public contract focuses on durable memory, catalog scope, lifecycle state, evidence, and retrieval rather than owning an entire generation stack.

How is MESA different from plain vector search?

Every result comes back with the document and passage it came from. Access rules are applied before ranking, four search methods are combined instead of one, and every change can be tracked and undone.

Why SQLite, LanceDB, and Kùzu?

SQLite owns catalog, authorization, ledgers, ownership, assertions, and outbox state. LanceDB stores the vector projection. Kùzu stores the Graph V2 projection and supports bounded graph-path retrieval reconciled to SQLite assertion IDs.

What does evidence-aware memory mean?

Retrieved knowledge can remain connected to document, revision, chunk, evidence span, assertion, pipeline, and embedding identity instead of returning only detached text.

What is provenance?

Provenance is the trace of where a memory came from and how it was processed: source reference, catalog identity, evidence span, pipeline and model versions, and contributing retrieval origins when available.

What is MESA Data?

A Turkish legal-data preparation platform. It preserves raw artifacts, canonicalizes records, applies gates and review, freezes releases, and uses a human-started delivery path. It is not advertised as a universal web ingestion service.

What is MESA Law?

The primary reference implementation: a legal matter and document workflow with source-aware review and a versioned MESA V4 HTTP contract. Its live Core/full-stack integration is still pending.

How do MESA QA and E2E Certification differ?

QA asks whether candidate behavior stays correct across time, sessions, and restarts. E2E Certification asks whether one frozen system profile can produce the required authoritative evidence and pass all hard gates.

Does MESA support MCP?

Yes. Run mesa start then mesa mcp-config for direct V4 stdio. Client tool approvals and key grants apply there; the HTTP gateway/bridge provides separate binding-scoped policy, audit and approvals.

Can MESA run locally?

Yes. Install mesa-memory[adapters] and run mesa start. Local credentials are automatic; mesa add and mesa search work through BM25 with models off. Models and graph are optional. Docker uses the same local CLI with persistent volume credentials.

Is MESA production-ready?

No. Core is a published source release and production remains NO-GO. Required production-like migration, restore, crash, saturation, concurrency, benchmark, and soak gates are not all complete.

What is the current certification status?

Not passed yet. The test harness is built, but some required evidence from external systems is still missing, so no fresh official run has passed. Details are on the status page.

Where should a developer start?

Follow the v0.9.0 quickstart: install the package, run mesa start, add a document and search it. Use Mesa() from Python or mesa mcp-config for MCP, then review the API, architecture and production limits.
